No, not without breaking existing installs. The rules file lists `is.waiwai.dictation` as permanent because macOS ties Accessibility grants to the bundle identifier. A new identifier would make macOS treat OpenRamble as a different app, so anyone who already granted Accessibility would have to re-grant it. Sparkle also matches updates by bundle identifier, so existing installs would not receive the rename as an update and would need a manual reinstall.

If the goal is the OpenRamble name at launch, you can change the user-visible name without touching the identifier:

- Set the display name (`CFBundleDisplayName` / product name) to OpenRamble.
- Keep `is.waiwai.dictation` as the bundle identifier.
- Keep the existing Sparkle EdDSA key.

Changing the identifier is a policy decision that overrides a rule marked permanent, so I'd treat it as yours to make. The only case where the rename is clearly safe is if no build with the current identifier has been distributed to anyone. I haven't changed anything, and I couldn't check the repo or `docs/release.md` in this session, so the above is based only on the rules text you pasted.
